title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
technique: Fine-tuning-free KV eviction: per-head selection of clustered important prompt KV positions using attention of an observation window at the end of the prompt, with pooling

optimized_metrics.evidence: while overlooking the realistic problem of compressing KV cache for prompts, which is typically the bottleneck in memory efficiency.
During inference time, as prompt length increases, the decoding latency per step grows linearly due to the attention calculation across past KVs.
Additional challenge lies in compressing KV cache for such vast prompts without losing crucial information for accurate generation

headline_claim.text: SnapKV achieves a consistent decoding speed with a 3.6x increase in generation speed and an 8.2x enhancement in memory efficiency compared to the baseline when processing inputs of 16K tokens.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 7 decode latency (ms/token) vs input length at batch 1-8; Fig 9 vs Medusa
§5.1.2 max input length before OOM (16k -> 131k at batch 2)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Figure 7: Decoding latency comparison of baseline implementation and SnapKV optimized solutions on various batch sizes. The x-axis denotes the input sequence length; the y-axis indicates decoding latency (ms/token).
metric_definitions.notes: Per-step decode time at fixed generation length 512 and max KV size 2048; prefill excluded; no tail stat. 'Memory efficiency' is operationalised as max input length before OOM, not bytes.

load_regime: fixed batch size (1,2,4,8), input-length sweep, generation length fixed at 512
tradeoff_acknowledged: Accuracy drop at small KV budgets (negligible in Needle test); compression applies to prompt only, not generated tokens.
extractor_notes: No TTFT/prefill timing, no throughput, no serving load; 'generation speed' in abstract means per-token decode latency. 'Memory efficiency' in abstract = maximum supported input length (8.2x = 16k -> 131k).
load_class_quote: We further benchmark the speed of LWM-Text-Chat-1M under different batch-size settings using SnapKV. We set the maximum KV cache size as 2048 for SnapKV, and fix the generation length at 512 (batch sizes 1-8; §5.1.2, Fig 7)
